title: Composite bow
summary: Laminated wood, horn, and sinew made compact bows suited to mounted archery.

parents.reason: Woodworking shaped the composite bow's wooden core and joined pieces into its curved form.
parents.directContribution: Woodworking shaped the wood core and joined the laminated bow; animal horn and sinew supplied separate mechanical properties.

title: Longbow
summary: Tall self bows stored energy along a long stave for hunting and warfare.

parents.reason: Woodworking shaped the long, gradually bending stave used by a self bow.
parents.directContribution: Woodworking formed the long flexible stave itself; the wider bow-and-arrow system separately names the type of launcher and projectile.

title: Sling weapon
summary: Two-cord slings extended the distance at which people could throw stones and shaped projectiles.

parents.reason: Plant-fiber cordage and woven pouches supplied the flexible cradle used to launch sling projectiles.

title: Crossbow
summary: A trigger-held bow mounted on a stock let a shooter aim after spanning the string.

parents.reason: Woodworking supplied the tiller that mounted the bow and carried its trigger mechanism.
parents.directContribution: Woodworking made the tiller and stock, while cast bronze separately supplied working components in early Chinese trigger assemblies.

parents.reason: Cast bronze components formed the Chinese crossbow trigger assembly that retained and released the drawn string.
parents.directContribution: Bronze supplied the working trigger pieces in early Chinese crossbows; shaping the wooden tiller was a separate structural contribution.

title: Mounted archery
summary: Mounted archers combined mobility with shooting bows from horseback.

parents.reason: Domesticated horses provided the mounts from which mobile archers fought.
Compact composite bows enabled effective archery from horseback across steppe warfare traditions.
parents.directContribution: The Scythian-style composite bow was specifically suited to mounted archery; domesticated horses independently supplied the mobile platform.

title: Mechanical catapult
summary: Mechanical siege engines stored energy to launch projectiles beyond hand-thrown range.

title: Counterweight trebuchet
summary: A falling counterweight swung a throwing arm to launch heavy siege projectiles.

title: Mail armor
summary: Interlinked iron or steel rings formed flexible protective clothing for soldiers.

parents.reason: Smelted iron supplied the metal worked into the linked rings of early mail armor.

title: Full plate armor
summary: Articulated metal plates covered most of a wearer's body while allowing movement.

parents.reason: Iron-carbon steel supplied the plates used in late medieval full suits of armor.
Full plate suits developed from transitional armor worn over mail, retaining mail in joints and gaps.

title: European cannon
wiki: Gunpowder artillery in the Middle Ages
summary: European armies used primitive cannons at the Battle of Crécy in 1346 as gunpowder artillery entered battlefield warfare.

parents.reason: Gunpowder supplied the propellant used by European cannons in battlefield service.

title: Hand cannon
summary: Portable metal-barrel firearms extended gunpowder weapons to individual soldiers.

parents.reason: Gunpowder supplied the propellant that made early metal-barrel hand firearms possible.

title: Matchlock firearm
summary: A trigger-linked holder brought a smoldering match to a firearm's priming charge.

parents.reason: Matchlocks added a trigger-operated ignition mechanism to the earlier hand cannon.

title: Firearm barrel rifling
summary: Spiral grooves in a firearm barrel stabilized projectiles and improved accuracy.

title: Flintlock firearm
summary: A flint-striking lock replaced the continuously burning match as a firearm's ignition source.

title: Breech-loading firearm
summary: Loading a firearm from the rear of its barrel reduced the time and space required to reload.

title: Percussion-cap ignition
summary: A struck percussion cap gave muzzle-loading firearms a compact, weather-resistant ignition source.

title: Self-contained firearm cartridge
summary: Pauly and Prelat developed an integrated cartridge in 1808, combining the ammunition into a unit loaded through a firearm breech.

parents.reason: Pauly designed the integrated cartridge for loading through the rear chamber of a breech-loading firearm.

title: Cartridge-fed repeating rifles
summary: Metallic-cartridge repeating rifles entered American Civil War service in the early 1860s, allowing multiple shots between reloads.

parents.reason: Compact cartridges could be stored and fed from magazines or cylinders for repeated firing.

title: Gatling mechanical rapid-fire gun
summary: The 1862 Gatling design mechanized repeated ammunition feeding while remaining hand-powered; fully automatic machine guns followed later.

title: Smokeless firearm propellant
summary: Smokeless propellant reduced battlefield smoke and fouling and enabled automatic firearms.

title: Bastion fortification
summary: Low, thick angled fortifications reduced cannon damage and covered defensive blind spots.

parents.reason: European cannon fire made tall medieval masonry walls vulnerable, prompting lower and thicker angled bastion defenses.

title: Roman legion
summary: The Roman legion organized citizen soldiers into the Republic’s principal military unit; its exact early formation date remains uncertain.

title: Cohort-based Roman legion
summary: Late Republican reforms organized Roman legions into ten cohorts for sustained field service.

parents.reason: The cohort structure reorganized the established Roman legion into ten larger tactical subunits.

title: Neo-Assyrian standing army
summary: Tiglath-Pileser III's reign began in 745 BCE and developed a permanent professional force able to serve beyond seasonal campaigns.

title: Mass national conscription
summary: Revolutionary France mobilized eligible citizens through near-universal national military service.

title: Institutional military logistics
summary: Dedicated officers planned troop movement, camps, supply, and equipment support for armies.

title: Military academy
summary: Formal schools trained officers for military engineering, artillery, and command service.

title: Professional general staff
summary: Specialized staff officers coordinated planning, intelligence, logistics, and personnel for field commands.

parents.reason: Graduation from the Prussian Staff College was a prerequisite for appointment to the Prussian General Staff.

title: Military aviation
summary: Military forces used airborne observation and later powered aircraft for reconnaissance and combat roles.

parents.reason: The French observation balloon used at Fleurus in 1794 provided the first documented military aviation capability.

title: Dreadnought battleship
summary: All-big-gun battleships paired heavy armament with steam-turbine propulsion.

parents.reason: Steam turbines provided the propulsion system used in HMS Dreadnought's revolutionary 1906 design.

title: Full-deck aircraft carrier
summary: HMS Argus became the first aircraft carrier with a full-length flight deck for wheeled aircraft to take off and land.

parents.reason: The full-length deck was designed to launch and recover powered wheeled aircraft at sea.

title: Radio ship-detection experiment
summary: Hülsmeyer demonstrated radio-wave detection of ships in fog, but his 1904 instrument could not determine their distance and was rejected by military officials.

parents.reason: The Telemobiloscope transmitted radio waves and detected their reflection from a distant ship.

title: Tank
summary: Armored tracked vehicles crossed difficult ground while carrying weapons and crews.

parents.reason: The internal-combustion engine enabled rapid movement of the heavy armored vehicles developed during the First World War.

title: V-2 ballistic rocket
summary: The V-2 became the first practical modern ballistic missile and a suborbital launch vehicle.

parents.reason: Liquid-fuel propulsion powered the V-2's ascent and made it capable of suborbital flight.

title: R-7 Semyorka missile
summary: The first successful ICBM design was adapted into the Sputnik and Vostok launch vehicles.

parents.reason: The R-7 used liquid oxygen and kerosene propulsion to deliver its payload on an intercontinental trajectory.

title: Redstone ballistic missile
summary: The U.S. Army's Redstone missile continued V-2 engineering and later supported early U.S. crewed spaceflight.

parents.reason: Redstone was a direct descendant of the V-2, developed by a team that included German V-2 engineers brought to the United States.
Liquid-fueled rocket propulsion powered the Redstone missile and its later space-launch derivatives.
parents.directContribution: Liquid-fuel propulsion powered Redstone's flight; the V-2 separately supplied a direct engineering lineage.

title: Atlas intercontinental missile
summary: The Atlas was the first operational U.S. ICBM and later served as a family of orbital launch vehicles.

parents.reason: Liquid-fuel rocket propulsion supplied the Atlas missile's long-range ascent and was retained in its launch-vehicle derivatives.
parents.directContribution: Liquid-fuel propulsion supplied the Atlas's launch capability, while the missile's airframe and stage architecture were directly reused in space launchers.

title: Spear
summary: Wooden shafts with sharpened ends or attached points extended human reach in hunting and combat.

title: Spear-thrower
summary: A lever extended the thrower's reach and increased the energy imparted to a dart or spear.

parents.reason: Spear-throwers extended a hand-thrown spear or dart's launch distance and velocity.

title: Bow and arrow
summary: Likely arrowheads found at Sibudu Cave point to a bow-and-arrow system by about 60,000 years ago.

parents.reason: Woodworking shaped bows and arrow shafts into the elastic launcher and projectile system.

title: Massed English longbow warfare
summary: English and Welsh forces used massed longbow archers in major battles of the Hundred Years’ War.

parents.reason: English and Welsh forces used massed longbow archers at battles including Crécy in 1346.

title: Sputnik orbital launch vehicle
summary: The Sputnik-PS launch vehicle adapted the R-7 design to place Sputnik 1 into orbit.

parents.reason: Sputnik-PS was a derivative of the R-7 Semyorka adapted for the first satellite launch.

title: Vostok-K crewed launch vehicle
summary: The Vostok-K variant modified an R-7-derived launch vehicle for crewed missions, first flying in 1960 and launching Yuri Gagarin in 1961.

parents.reason: The R-7 core and strap-on booster architecture supplied the lower-stage platform adapted for the crew-rated Vostok-K.

title: Mercury-Redstone launch vehicle
summary: A crew-rated Redstone derivative launched the first American astronauts on suborbital Mercury flights.

parents.reason: The Mercury-Redstone design used the Jupiter-C first stage as its starting vehicle for crewed suborbital flight.
The latest military Redstone supplied the engine selected for the crewed Mercury booster.
parents.directContribution: The Redstone missile supplied the A-7 engine and the flight history of an established propulsion unit, while the Jupiter-C supplied the starting first-stage vehicle architecture.

title: Prussian Staff College
summary: Prussia re-founded a staff college to educate and train officers for General Staff appointments.

title: Chain Home early-warning radar
summary: Britain’s Chain Home network provided operational coastal warning and tracking of incoming aircraft.

parents.reason: The Chain Home stations transmitted radio waves and detected their reflections from aircraft to provide early warning.

title: Jupiter-C research launch vehicle
summary: A modified Redstone research vehicle tested reentry systems and led to the Juno I satellite launcher.

parents.reason: Jupiter-C was a modified Redstone ballistic missile with additional upper stages for research flights.
